with KAP Minerals on Tuesday to evaluate the processing of mineralized material from NTMFF's Hecla-Kilmer project at KAP's proposed Critical Minerals Processing Centre in Kapuskasing, Ontario.

The principal objective of the MOU is to assess the technical and commercial feasibility of Hecla-Kilmer phosphate and rare earth element bearing material at the Kapuskasing Processing Centre, including a potential future toll processing agreement.

"This agreement is about moving Hecla-Kilmer from an exploration story to a processing story," said Reagan Glazier, Neotech Metals’ CEO. "Governments and industrial partners have been clear on what they want from the critical minerals sector: a credible route from deposit to product, built in Canada. Pairing Hecla-Kilmer with planned processing infrastructure in Northern Ontario is exactly that kind of practical, capital efficient step," he added.

The processing centre is designed to produce multiple critical mineral products, using its existing mineral resources, industrial infrastructure, and planned beneficiation capabilities. The MOU also supports KAP's strategy to accommodate third-party mineral feedstock.

"By attracting additional feedstock, we can improve plant utilization, strengthen project economics and accelerate the development of a globally competitive Canadian critical minerals supply chain," said C. Geoff Hampson, KAP Minerals’ CEO.
The term of the MOU is 12 months from execution and is extendable by mutual written agreement. Either party may terminate the agreement on 30 days' written notice.

title: Neotech Metals, KAP Minerals sign MOU to assess Hecla-Kilmer material processing at proposed Kapuskasing facility
